trust_decision.summary: VFS decides who owns the mount-point reference (parent mount + point dentry) of a lazily/partly umounted mount, and whether a detached (umounted) mount may be used as a bind source; at the pinned commit umount drops the whole mount-point ref early, and later disconnects of the partly-umounted mount drop nothing for the dentry, so the point dentry ref count is wrong (UAF / double put), and BindAt accepts an umounted nsfs/cgroupfs source.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names 'VFS MemoryFile' double free, so a summary-only reader goes to the MemoryFile allocator; none of the fix commits touch it. A reader who knows the area lands on umountTreeLocked (pkg/sentry/vfs/mount.go:986).

fix_sites.entry_point: umount2(2) with MNT_DETACH -> UmountAt -> umountTreeLocked (also InvalidateDentry -> forgetDeadMountpoint -> umountTreeLocked)
unlink/rmdir/rename or filesystem revalidation of a mount point -> VirtualFilesystem.InvalidateDentry -> forgetDeadMountpoint

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/sentry/vfs/dentry.go:343-347 (forgetDeadMountpoint, reached from InvalidateDentry on file deletion, not from umount) and pkg/sentry/vfs/mount.go:1224-1231 (Mount.destroy child cleanup)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The comments at pkg/sentry/vfs/dentry.go:341-342 and pkg/sentry/vfs/mount.go:1220-1221 explicitly assert 'the mount point has already been decrefed by umount', so a solver who rebalances only umountTreeLocked can argue the destroy/forgetDeadMountpoint paths are already correct by design.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Locked children of a lazily umounted parent must stay connected (partly umounted) and keep the parent alive until its last reference drops; nsfs/cgroupfs/cgroup2fs mounts from another namespace must stay bindable non-recursively. An over-broad fix that always disconnects, or rejects all non-namespace bind sources, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: lazy umount (MNT_DETACH) of a parent with a locked child, child later disconnected by parent destroy
same, child later disconnected by mount-point invalidation (forgetDeadMountpoint)
non-recursive MS_BIND of a detached nsfs/cgroupfs/cgroup2fs mount
recursive MS_BIND|MS_REC of a mount outside the namespace (exemption removed for recursive)

O7_producer.where: Reference ownership is produced by connectLocked (pkg/sentry/vfs/mount.go:1101-1127) and consumed by disconnectLocked (pkg/sentry/vfs/mount.go:1136-1164); no schema/serializer involved.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: commitMount disconnects an existing child at the target point and drops its full mount-point ref; a partly umounted child found by mounts.Lookup would be double-put on the parent mount after the fix.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Partly umounted mounts stay in the mount hash table and the guard against mounting on umounted parents lives elsewhere (pkg/sentry/vfs/mount.go:453, pkg/sentry/vfs/propagation.go:269); removing or omitting one of those guards is a plausible maintainer slip.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: changeMountpoint drops the full old key; if called on an umounted-but-connected mount the parent ref is dropped twice.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same disconnect-and-decref idiom used in umount propagation reparenting; a maintainer extending propagateUmount to restore umounted mounts would hit it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: MoveMountAt submount disconnect drops the full old key without considering partly umounted state.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Move path checks umounted on the source (pkg/sentry/vfs/mount.go:592) but a variant lacking that check would be a natural sibling.

O9_family: memory safety / reference-count imbalance (use-after-free, double put) in Go refcounted VFS objects
